tier_reason: README tables are first-party and come from public criterion harnesses (app/benches/gauss/main.rs, stack_blur/main.rs, median/main.rs, using the opencv crate 0.98.1), but no CPU model, OpenCV version/build or rustc flags are stated (toolchain is unpinned nightly), so not A. Only the RGB and single-plane Gaussian rows are backed by a harness that matches its label closely; the stack-blur, RGBA and median rows rest on harness bugs or code that does not produce them.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Gaussian blur, 3000x4000 RGB 8-bit, multithreaded (harness uses kernel 155 with sigma 25.83 for both libraries although the README says 151): libblur Exact 49.40 ms (NEON) and 43.41 ms (AVX) versus OpenCV 180.56 ms and 182.44 ms, about 3.7x and 4.2x (derived from page data); libblur FixedPoint, which the README says adds 1-3% error, 26.68 ms and 30.72 ms, about 6.8x and 5.9x (derived). Single plane 3000x4000: Exact 17.59 ms and 15.51 ms versus OpenCV 74.73 ms and 64.20 ms, about 4.2x and 4.1x (derived). The RGBA Gaussian rows (65.13/51.40 ms versus 134.60/185.30 ms) and stack-blur rows (RGB 4.95/5.30 ms versus 8.43/10.36 ms, about 1.7x and 2.0x derived) time OpenCV on a 2-channel BGR565 Mat because of a cvtColor argument bug, and the median rows (RGB 603.51/872.03 ms versus 637.83/959.07 ms, about 1.06x and 1.10x derived) are not produced by the public median harness.
corrections.caveats: First-party README tables with no CPU model (machines labelled only NEON and AVX/SSE), no OpenCV version or build options, no thread count and no rustc flags (rust-toolchain.toml says nightly). Harness review (app/benches): (1) Gaussian RGB is the cleanest comparison: both sides use kernel 155 and sigma 25.83 (README labels it 151) and both are threaded; OpenCV runs with ALGO_HINT_ACCURATE, which in OpenCV 4.x selects the bit-exact fixed-point SIMD path (parallel_for_) and skips the HAL and IPP approximate paths, so the libblur FixedPoint figures (1-3% error) compare an approximation against a bit-exact result; borders differ (libblur Clamp versus OpenCV BORDER_DEFAULT reflect-101) and OpenCV allocates a new 36 MB destination Mat inside the timed loop while libblur reuses a preallocated buffer. (2) The single-plane Exact run uses kernel 151 against OpenCV's 155. (3) Every 'RGBA' and 'RGB' OpenCV input built with cvt_color(&src, &mut dst, CV_8UC3, CV_8UC4, ...) passes CV_8UC3 (=16) as the conversion code, which is COLOR_BGRA2BGR565, so OpenCV actually blurs a 2-channel 8-bit Mat: the RGBA Gaussian rows and both stack-blur rows compare OpenCV on 2 bytes per pixel against libblur on 3-4 bytes per pixel. (4) Stack blur: OpenCV is called with Size(77,77), i.e. radius 38, while libblur uses radius 77, and libblur's RGB run is given the 2828x4242 dimensions of test_image_4.png for the 3000x4000 buffer of test_image_1.jpg (same byte count, wrong geometry), matching the stride and label bugs seen in the author's sparkyuv and yuvutils-rs harnesses. (5) The public median harness (updated 2026-05-05) is single-threaded with radius 1-4 and compares libblur on test_image_2.png (720x1080 RGBA) against OpenCV on test_image_4.png (2828x4242 loaded as 3-channel), so it cannot have produced the README's multithreaded radius-35 median table. Median gain is 3-16% at best (derived). 'Gaussian blur in 100 FPS for 4K photo' is directional. Rust crate with a cbindgen C API.

notes: Real Gaussian win of about 4x for the Exact mode on RGB and single plane is supported by a harness with matching kernel and sigma, but the stack-blur, RGBA and median rows are mislabelled or unbacked (cvtColor code bug makes OpenCV inputs 2-channel; median harness does different work), so the claim was narrowed to the Gaussian rows; tier stays C. License (Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause), last commit 2026-05-08 and active status confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party tables in quantette/docs/Benchmarks and Accuracy.md, produced by the public harness quantette/examples/cli.rs with -C target-feature=+avx2, but no CPU model or rustc version is stated, so not A. The only third-party timing (imazen/zenquant README) is a competitor's approximate multi-threaded run whose own methodology doc says its ~ms column is not for timing claims, so it does not lift the entry to B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Own harness, 256 colours, 4 threads for quantette and imagequant, no dithering: quantette k-means (quality comparable to imagequant by the doc's DSSIM table) is 3.3x to 14.1x faster than imagequant 4.4.1 at default settings on the eleven 5-6.7k-wide photos (median about 7.6x; Akihabara 97 ms versus 1044 ms, about 10.8x) and 2.9x to 8.6x on the 1920-wide versions (median about 4.9x), all derived from page data. With dithering the gap is 1.13x to 5.1x on the large photos (Futuristic 318 ms versus 360 ms; median about 2.6x) and 3.3x to 8.4x at 1920 wide (derived). Wu sRGB (25 ms on Akihabara, 8x to 46x faster than imagequant) produces clearly worse output (DSSIM 0.0072 versus 0.0044 on Akihabara), so its ratio is not a like-for-like speedup. In the imazen/zenquant README (50 images, 2026-03-04, default dithering, approximate timing) quantette 0.5 k-means takes about 265 ms versus imagequant 315 ms at speed 4 and 546 ms at speed 1, about 1.2x and 2.1x (derived), and color_quant is faster than both at 180 ms.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are in quantette/docs/Benchmarks and Accuracy.md (file last edited 2025-12-23, so they predate quantette 0.6.0); CPU model and rustc version are not stated. Harness quantette/examples/cli.rs times one quantize+remap per process (30 runs averaged) with --verbose; image decode and imagequant's new_image setup are outside the timed region. Workloads differ: imagequant quantizes RGBA with alpha handling while quantette only supports RGB; imagequant ran at its library defaults (speed 4, quality target 100, dither level 0.0 in the no-dither runs); quantette k-means uses default KmeansOptions (sampled mini-batch k-means, iteration count not stated in the doc). The headline single-image ratio (about 10.8x on Akihabara) is near the top of a 3.3x to 14.1x range, and the gap shrinks to 1.13x on Futuristic with dithering. In imazen/zenquant's comparison (a competitor's harness, quantette 0.5, default dithering) the gap is only about 1.2x to 2.1x, and that doc marks its ~ms column as approximate (multi-threaded across images) and not for timing claims. The author notes each library has options that change results.

notes: Numbers in the record match the benchmark doc and the comparison is against the named incumbent (imagequant), but the headline picked a near-best-case image and a quality-mismatched Wu ratio; claim restated as ranges with the dithering and zenquant results, tier stays C.
